triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as a pure identifier rename or an architecture-only "input surface generalization" and could not: within this one file at the parent commit, `entry_is_line_a` simultaneously zeroes the §122 surcharge (line 2572) and carries China-301 list-1 membership (line 2994), and `entry_is_line_b` simultaneously zeroes §122, gates §232 aluminum (2744/2751) and gates the China-301 2024 action (2995), so no caller population of those booleans can make all the rules correct at chapter scale — the fix splits one flag into several distinct identifiers rather than renaming it. The §122 rule's own exception atoms cite only the 9903.03.03 subdivision (aa)(ii) exclusion list, 7202.11.10, and the "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles" carve-out; nothing in the cited source exempts §301-listed lines from the surcharge, so the pre-fix condition was a branch with no source basis and the fix re-grounds it to the two cited exception predicates. That is untraceable_branch rather than wrong_entity_or_scope or polarity_or_logic: the ungrounded thing is the condition itself, and the repair is re-grounding it on the provision the rule already cites. Mechanical is ruled out because formula tokens and runtime values change (the PR concedes a "principled exception class" of 18 witness-slice cells that differ precisely where "the witness's own coupling was the unlawful part").

triage.verifier_notes:
inferred from verified sibling module index 72 (same kind and rule path in this chunk). Corroboration is structural, not just narrative: at parent 29dbbdac05, `git show 29dbbdac05:us/policies/cbp/us-tariff-schedule/generated/ch73/ch73.yaml` line 2572 zeroes §122 on `entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b` while line 2994 uses `entry_is_line_a` as China-301 list-1 membership and 2995 uses `entry_is_line_b` as the 2024-action membership. The "unlawfully suppressed" wording is self-reported PR text from the same authoring agent (Claude Fable 5), so I leaned on the diff rather than the claim.

Caveats a reviewer should weigh:
1. The fix is partial. Post-fix the exemplar flags survive at lines 1908 (`entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded: formula: entry_is_line_a`), 1925 (`entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded: formula: entry_is_line_b`), 2368/2524 (`if origin_is_brazil and not entry_is_line_b` in the IEEPA reciprocal stack) and 2998 (`entry_is_line_d and origin_is_china` in the 301 sum). This does not make the repaired branch a non-defect, but the module is not fully decoupled.
2. The same diff bundles a second, separable change: new `ch73_s232_steel_heading_rate` (0.50) + `section_232_steel_component_rate`, wired into `schedule_statutory_stack`. That is added coverage (unrepresented_clause at best, or an enhancement outside the module's declared "same panel-projection component sequence as the witness total" scope), and per the PR it is the larger numeric effect (3.89pp). If the corpus wants one defect per module, the §122 re-grounding is the anchored and better-evidenced one; if it allows multiple, the steel component should be scored separately.
3. The Brazil and forced-labor rewrites are a different flavor again — they drop an ungrounded a/b exclusion *and* add a missing membership gate (`entry_is_brazil_301_listed`, `entry_is_forced_labor_301_listed`), with those inputs defaulting FALSE per the summary. Arguably unrepresented_clause for the added list gate.
4. The §201 CSPV hunk (`if entry_is_line_e: 0 else: 0` -> `if entry_is_section_201_cspv: 0 else: 0`) is runtime-inert — both branches return 0 — so it carries no fidelity weight.
5. Provenance check: through the pinned release `us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap` (corpus commit e79781bd), `us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-221` resolves to note subdivisions (x)-(z) and page-230 to §232 steel TRQ notes — neither contains the (aa)(ii) 9903.03.03 excerpt or the "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper" excerpt the §122 atoms quote. Those atoms are unchanged by this diff (page indexing appears to have shifted between HTS revisions), so it does not affect the verdict, but a reviewer relying on atom excerpt/page alignment should not treat those paths as verified.
